title: The knot's count reads the Euler characteristic and is blind to orientation
subject: Whether the surface carrying a knot space decides whether the knot's count forces a contradiction, and in which class
conclusion: On every closed surface, violated lines minus the faces' excess agreements equals (chi - |D|)/2, where D, the faces the signs make even, has the parity of chi, so the count forces a violated line only on the sphere with Kasteleyn signs and forces an over-agreeing face when chi < |D|. Orientation never enters, and wherever the count forces, the search lies in PPADS^dt, so unlike Sperner it never becomes PPA-hard on non-orientable surfaces.
